title: Morning Headlines
intro: A bipartisan House rebellion against Trump's foreign policy, North Korea's latest nuclear escalation, and a landmark legal case for a former national security advisor headline a packed Thursday in global news.

items.title: House Defies Trump, Passes Ukraine Aid and Russia Sanctions Package
items.subtitle: CNN / PBS NewsHour / ABC News
items.summary: Eighteen House Republicans crossed the aisle to pass a $9.8 billion Ukraine security package — including military loans and sweeping new oil-and-gas sanctions on Russia — in a 226–195 vote that openly rebuffed President Trump. The White House vowed an immediate veto, but the bipartisan revolt marks the sharpest congressional challenge yet to Trump's stance on the war in Ukraine.

items.title: North Korea Unveils New Nuclear Fuel Plant; Kim Vows 'Exponential' Weapons Buildup
items.subtitle: NPR / CNN
items.summary: Kim Jong Un inspected a newly disclosed uranium enrichment facility and declared that North Korea's nuclear materials production capacity has more than doubled in five years, pledging to expand it exponentially. South Korea's military assessed the site as a weapons-grade uranium plant and said it is coordinating closely with the U.S. to monitor the escalation.

items.title: John Bolton Agrees to Plead Guilty to Retaining Classified Information
items.subtitle: CNN / The Washington Post
items.summary: Former National Security Advisor John Bolton has reached a plea deal, agreeing to plead guilty to retaining classified national-security details in a private diary that he shared with his wife and daughter — both without security clearances. Bolton faces up to five years in prison and a $2.25 million fine at his June 26 court hearing.

items.title: Senate Passes Reconciliation Bill Locking In Three Years of ICE Funding
items.subtitle: CBS News
items.summary: After a marathon 'vote-a-rama,' the Senate approved a reconciliation measure guaranteeing three years of dedicated ICE funding without an accompanying DOJ spending ban, delivering a major win for the administration's immigration enforcement agenda. The bill advances toward final congressional passage.

items.title: Super Typhoon Sinlaku Triggers Atmospheric Gravity Waves Visible From Space
items.subtitle: NASA Earth Observatory / ScienceDaily
items.summary: Satellites captured rare atmospheric gravity waves rippling outward from Super Typhoon Sinlaku — the strongest Pacific tropical cyclone of 2026 — as it rapidly intensified to Category 5 equivalent, with the waves spreading like concentric rings far into the upper atmosphere. Scientists say the event offers an unprecedented view of how extreme storms can disturb the atmosphere at global scale.
